reference.label: fibre cut
reference.definition: A physical break in a fibre span that prevents optical signals from passing.
reference.example: Construction severs an upstream span, leaving the next amplifier with no input light.

reference.label: span loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in fibre-span attenuation, such as from a bend, splice, or stressed cable, that reduces downstream power.
reference.example: A cable bend adds 10 dB of span loss and causes the receiving channel power to fall.

reference.label: disconnected optical connector
reference.definition: A connector or patch cord is disconnected, interrupting the optical path at that point.
reference.example: A technician unplugs the launch patch cord and all downstream receivers lose light.

reference.label: dirty optical connector
reference.definition: Contamination on an optical connector adds loss or reflection and degrades the carried signal.
reference.example: Cleaning a contaminated patch-panel connector restores received power and OSNR.

reference.label: amplifier outage
reference.definition: Failure of an optical amplifier or its pump that results in no usable amplifier output.
reference.example: A failed inline amplifier receives light but emits none toward the next span.

reference.label: amplifier gain drop
reference.definition: An amplifier's gain falls below its configured set point, weakening its output channels.
reference.example: An amplifier commissioned for 17 dB gain delivers only 14 dB.

reference.label: amplifier noise increase
reference.definition: An amplifier introduces a larger optical-noise penalty, reducing OSNR even when signal power remains normal.
reference.example: An upstream amplifier adds ASE noise and lowers OSNR on every carried channel.

reference.label: amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: An amplifier's gain varies excessively across the optical band rather than remaining spectrally flat.
reference.example: Long-wavelength channels leave an amplifier 2 dB weaker than central channels.

reference.label: pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive amplifier-pump ageing that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain.
reference.example: Pump drive rises from 100% to 121% of its commissioning value over several months.

reference.label: transmit-laser failure
reference.definition: A terminal's transmit laser fails or stops emitting a usable optical signal.
reference.example: A laser-driver failure extinguishes the wavelength seen by the far-end receiver.

reference.label: equipment card failure
reference.definition: A hardware card or terminal module fails, preventing its normal traffic and monitoring functions.
reference.example: A failed wavelength-terminal card carries no traffic and stops reporting telemetry.

reference.label: receiver degradation
reference.definition: A local coherent receiver adds a signal penalty without impairing the upstream route or other receivers.
reference.example: A defective receiver DSP produces errors while neighbouring channels remain healthy.

reference.label: transmit-laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive laser ageing evidenced by increasing transmit bias required to maintain output.
reference.example: A transmitter's laser bias rises to 125% of its commissioning value.

reference.label: channel margin erosion
reference.definition: A gradual decline in an optical channel's remaining reception margin.
reference.example: A channel loses 0.2 dB of OSNR margin per month until errors begin.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A wavelength-selective switch's attenuation setting or effective loss changes for one channel.
reference.example: A WSS attenuation drift makes one routed channel 3 dB weaker.

reference.label: uncompensated channel attenuation
reference.definition: A channel power deficit exceeds a router's available equalization or attenuation-compensation range.
reference.example: A channel arriving 12 dB low remains 4 dB below target after an 8 dB correction.

reference.label: WSS passband shift
reference.definition: A WSS filter passband is offset from a channel and clips or narrows its spectrum.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband clips one channel while its measured power remains normal.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of one WSS directional input blocks all channels entering through that port.
reference.example: Failure of the east input stops east-originated channels while other directions continue.

reference.label: DGD increase
reference.definition: Differential group delay increases on an optical path and reduces receiver recoverability.
reference.example: DGD rises beyond the coherent receiver's compensation tolerance.

reference.label: polarisation transient
reference.definition: A rapid change in optical state of polarisation that may outrun receiver tracking.
reference.example: Movement of an aerial fibre causes rapid polarisation rotation and bursts of errors.

reference.label: mechanical disturbance
reference.definition: A brief physical disturbance of fibre or patching that produces a transient optical loss excursion.
reference.example: Work on a patch panel causes a one-second received-power dip.

reference.label: channel-loading transient
reference.definition: Adding or removing channels causes a brief aggregate or per-channel optical-power excursion.
reference.example: Adding several channels to an OMS briefly depresses the power of existing channels.

reference.label: protection-switch interruption
reference.definition: A protection selector's route change briefly interrupts the protected service.
reference.example: Switching from the working route to protection causes a 50 ms client interruption.

reference.label: OTN switching-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric prevents normal switching of the affected ODUs.
reference.example: A failed fabric card interrupts every ODU switched through it.

reference.label: cross-connect misconnection
reference.definition: An incorrectly provisioned OTN cross-connect delivers an ODU to the wrong destination.
reference.example: An ODU intended for client A is mapped to client B's port.

reference.label: client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a customer-facing client port or its optic interrupts the attached service.
reference.example: A failed tributary optic cuts the customer service while the line remains operational.

reference.label: instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring instrument reports a value that does not represent the actual measured state.
reference.example: A power monitor reports −20 dBm although an independent meter reads −10 dBm.

reference.label: stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitoring source continues reporting an old frozen value instead of current measurements.
reference.example: The reported channel power remains fixed for an hour despite real power changes.

reference.label: unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure earlier on the active signal path that accounts for a downstream defect.
reference.example: Received AIS is attributed to an upstream path failure until a specific fault is found.

reference.label: unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure in a server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: An ODU outage is attributed generically to a failed supporting OTU or optical layer.

reference.label: incorrect service provisioning
reference.definition: Provisioning parameters or associations do not implement the intended service path.
reference.example: An operator maps a client ODU to the wrong cross-connect output during turn-up.

reference.label: optical signal loss
reference.definition: No usable optical signal reaches a receiver, or its power is below the detection threshold.
reference.example: A cut upstream span leaves the landing amplifier with zero input power.

reference.label: low optical power
reference.definition: Optical signal power is below its expected or required level but may still be detectable.
reference.example: A channel arrives at −23 dBm and has insufficient receiver margin.

reference.label: supervisory-channel loss
reference.definition: The optical supervisory channel is absent on a span whose supervisory link is locally terminated.
reference.example: A downstream amplifier loses the OSC from its immediately preceding span.

reference.label: optical power excursion
reference.definition: Optical power undergoes a brief dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Received power falls by 4 dB for half a second and then recovers.

reference.label: low OSNR
reference.definition: A channel's optical signal-to-noise ratio is reduced enough to impair signal quality.
reference.example: A channel with normal power but 8 dB OSNR produces pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: fast polarisation change
reference.definition: The received state of polarisation changes faster than the receiver can reliably track.
reference.example: A rapid SOP change produces several errored seconds.
synonyms: polarisation swings faster than the tracker

reference.label: high DGD
reference.definition: Received differential group delay is elevated beyond the receiver's usable compensation margin.
reference.example: A receiver reports 80 ps DGD and begins losing frames.

reference.label: optical filter penalty
reference.definition: Spectral narrowing or passband misalignment degrades a channel even though its total power may remain normal.
reference.example: A clipped modulation sideband raises errors while received power stays at target.

reference.label: receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: Signal degradation originates within one local receiver and does not propagate along the route.
reference.example: Only one receiver reports errors on an otherwise healthy lightpath.

reference.label: unit down
reference.definition: An equipment unit has failed, carries no traffic, and supplies no valid monitoring values.
reference.example: A failed line card loses traffic and stops reporting power and temperature.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: A line receiver can no longer recover or align to the Optical Transport Unit frame.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes the receiver to lose OTU framing.

reference.label: degraded OTU
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation threshold while OTU frame alignment remains intact.
reference.example: The pre-FEC ratio crosses 1×10^-3 but the receiver remains frame-aligned.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An ODU AIS replacement signal travels downstream to indicate an upstream failure.
reference.example: A tributary receives ODU AIS from an upstream terminal and declares AIS reception.

reference.label: misrouted ODU
reference.definition: An ODU is delivered to a destination other than the one for which it was provisioned.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT-A receives the trace identity for CLIENT-B.

reference.label: client service down
reference.definition: A client service is unavailable in the affected direction.
reference.example: No customer frames pass through the tributary after its client optic fails.

reference.label: brief client interruption
reference.definition: A client service is interrupted briefly, commonly while protection selection changes routes.
reference.example: The customer sees a 50 ms traffic break during protection switching.

reference.label: rising amplifier pump drive
reference.definition: The pump current required to maintain amplifier gain is increasing over time.
reference.example: Pump drive trends from 100% to 115% over six months.

reference.label: rising transmit-laser bias
reference.definition: The bias current required by a transmit laser is increasing as the laser ages.
reference.example: Laser bias increases from 80 mA to 98 mA over several years.

reference.label: declining channel margin
reference.definition: The difference between current channel quality and the receiver failure threshold is decreasing gradually.
reference.example: A channel's OSNR margin falls from 5 dB to 1 dB over a year.

reference.label: standby route selected
reference.definition: A protected service is currently carried over its standby or protection ODU route.
reference.example: A working-route failure causes the receiving selector to carry traffic over route S.

reference.label: protection route unavailable
reference.definition: The standby ODU route is defective or unavailable, reducing service resilience.
reference.example: The working route remains active while AIS on the protection route removes redundancy.

reference.label: backward defect indication
reference.definition: A remote receiver reports back that the signal sent toward it is defective.
reference.example: The far-end receiver returns a defect indication after losing the forward OTU frame.

reference.label: amplifier input power
reference.definition: Total aggregate optical power measured at an amplifier input.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports aggregate input power of +2.4 dBm.
synonyms: aggregate optical power entering the module

reference.label: amplifier output power
reference.definition: Total aggregate optical power measured at an amplifier output.
reference.example: A booster amplifier reports aggregate output power of +19.0 dBm.
synonyms: aggregate optical power leaving the module

reference.label: relative pump current
reference.definition: Current amplifier pump drive expressed relative to its commissioning or beginning-of-life baseline.
reference.example: A reading of 118% means the pump requires 18% more drive than at commissioning.

reference.label: relative laser bias
reference.definition: Current transmitter-laser bias expressed relative to its commissioning or beginning-of-life baseline.
reference.example: A terminal reports laser bias at 123% of its commissioning value.

reference.label: ROADM channel power
reference.definition: Per-channel optical power measured by an optical channel monitor at a ROADM.
reference.example: The east-degree OCM measures channel 37 at −6.2 dBm.

reference.label: ROADM channel OSNR
reference.definition: Per-channel OSNR estimated by an optical channel monitor at a ROADM.
reference.example: A ROADM OCM estimates channel 37's OSNR as 16.1 dB.

reference.label: receiver optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a coherent line receiver for its received channel.
reference.example: A terminal receiver reports its channel at −12.3 dBm.

reference.label: 15-minute receiver-power statistic
reference.definition: Received optical power summarized in a 15-minute performance-monitoring bin.
reference.example: The last PM15 bin records average receiver power of −12.5 dBm.

reference.label: line errored seconds
reference.definition: Count of one-second intervals containing line-side traffic errors, typically in a 15-minute bin.
reference.example: A line receiver records 12 errored seconds in the current PM15 interval.

reference.label: client errored seconds
reference.definition: Count of one-second intervals containing errors in the monitored client service.
reference.example: A client port reports 18 errored seconds in the last 15-minute interval.

reference.label: client unavailable seconds
reference.definition: Count of seconds during which a client service is classified as unavailable.
reference.example: A two-minute client outage adds 120 unavailable seconds.

reference.label: receiver-estimated OSNR
reference.definition: Per-channel OSNR estimated by a coherent receiver's DSP.
reference.example: The coherent receiver estimates an OSNR of 14.8 dB.

reference.label: pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: Fraction of received bits found erroneous before forward-error correction.
reference.example: A terminal reports a pre-FEC bit error ratio of 4×10^-4.

reference.label: differential group delay
reference.definition: Differential group delay estimated for a received coherent optical channel.
reference.example: The receiver reports DGD of 32 ps.

reference.label: state-of-polarisation change rate
reference.definition: Rate at which the received optical state of polarisation changes.
reference.example: The receiver records a sharp SOP-rate spike during fibre movement.

reference.label: supervisory reception status
reference.definition: Status indicating whether an amplifier site currently receives its incoming supervisory channel.
reference.example: The status changes from received to absent after an upstream span cut.
synonyms: whether the supervisory link is being received

reference.label: alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor that produces alarm state but exposes no numerical measurement values.
reference.example: An OSC receiver raises loss-of-supervision without reporting optical power.

reference.label: optical amplifier
reference.definition: An optical line amplifier that increases aggregate optical signal power.
reference.example: An EDFA compensates for loss on the preceding fibre span.

reference.label: booster amplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the transmitting or launch end of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A booster raises ROADM output to the configured section launch power.

reference.label: inline amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier located at an intermediate line site between terminal nodes.
reference.example: An inline amplifier in shelter B amplifies the signal for the next span.

reference.label: preamplifier
reference.definition: An amplifier at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section before the next node.
reference.example: A preamplifier boosts span input before the receiving ROADM.

reference.label: coherent line interface
reference.definition: A coherent optical interface that terminates an optical channel and its line framing.
reference.example: A coherent line interface estimates OSNR and recovers the OTU frame.

reference.label: transponder
reference.definition: A line interface mapping one client signal onto one coherent optical wavelength.
reference.example: A transponder carries one 400G client over a single wavelength.

reference.label: muxponder
reference.definition: A line interface aggregating multiple client signals onto one optical wavelength.
reference.example: A muxponder combines four client ODUs onto one line channel.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A coherent line card that interfaces an optical channel to digital ODU switching.
reference.example: An OTN line card passes recovered ODUs into the cross-connect fabric.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: A reconfigurable optical node that independently routes wavelengths through WSS degrees.
reference.example: A ROADM sends one east-arriving channel north and another west.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: A network element whose digital fabric cross-connects ODUs between line and client interfaces.
reference.example: An OTN switch maps an ODU from a line card to a client port.

reference.label: client port
reference.definition: A customer-facing interface that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100G client port terminates a customer service and reports unavailable seconds.

reference.label: all optical channels
reference.definition: Every optical channel in the affected multiplexed signal or equipment context.
reference.example: Amplifier excess noise reduces OSNR on all channels in the band.

reference.label: one optical channel
reference.definition: A single optical wavelength considered independently of other multiplexed channels.
reference.example: A shifted WSS passband degrades one channel while others remain healthy.

reference.label: channel subset
reference.definition: Some but not all channels in a multiplexed signal, such as channels near one band edge.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens only the long-wavelength edge channels.

reference.label: one ROADM direction input
reference.definition: All channels entering a ROADM through one directional WSS input port.
reference.example: An east-port failure blocks every channel arriving from the east.
synonyms: all light entering on one direction

reference.label: equipment unit
reference.definition: The equipment unit itself, as distinct from the traffic it carries.
reference.example: Pump ageing is scoped to the amplifier unit.

reference.label: one receiver
reference.definition: Only the specified receiver, excluding the route and other receivers.
reference.example: A receiver-local penalty affects this receiver alone.

reference.label: all switched ODUs
reference.definition: Every ODU cross-connected through the affected switching context.
reference.example: A fabric-card failure interrupts all ODUs switched through that card.

reference.label: one ODU
reference.definition: A single Optical Data Unit within a system that may carry or switch many ODUs.
reference.example: Only the misprovisioned ODU reaches the wrong client port.

reference.label: one client service
reference.definition: The particular customer traffic service under observation.
reference.example: The protection switch briefly interrupts this client service.

reference.label: local reporting unit
reference.definition: The local equipment unit that raised the alarm or observed the condition.
reference.example: Pump end-of-life is reported at the inline amplifier in shelter 12.

reference.label: local reporting port
reference.definition: The local interface port against which an alarm or condition is reported.
reference.example: The client failure is reported against tributary port 2.

reference.label: immediately upstream span
reference.definition: The fibre span directly preceding the observing unit in signal direction.
reference.example: Supervisory loss points to the 80 km span feeding the landing amplifier.

reference.label: immediately upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The amplifier that launches into the span immediately preceding the observing unit.
reference.example: Failure of the upstream amplifier leaves the next site dark.

reference.label: optical-section input connection
reference.definition: The patch or connection at the launch input of an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: A disconnected OMS input patch removes all light from the section.
synonyms: patch lead at the section head

reference.label: upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The channel or WSS input at the immediately preceding ROADM on the signal path.
reference.example: The channel is already weak at the upstream ROADM output.

reference.label: upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any span, amplifier, patch, or ROADM point before the observing unit on the signal path.
reference.example: A dirty connector anywhere upstream can produce the local degradation.

reference.label: far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting the lightpath received by the local unit.
reference.example: Failure of the far-end transmitter leaves the local receiver dark.

reference.label: far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the signal transmitted by the local unit.
reference.example: The far-end receiver reports a defect in the locally transmitted signal.

reference.label: path from far end
reference.definition: The complete received-signal path from the far-end transmitter through the network to the local unit.
reference.example: A received defect may originate anywhere on the path from the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: either client endpoint
reference.definition: Either of the two client ports bounding an end-to-end service.
reference.example: The client fault is eventually located at the remote service endpoint.

reference.label: ODU-path cross-connect
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect traversed by the service's ODU path.
reference.example: A misconnection at the second path switch sends the ODU to the wrong endpoint.

reference.label: working ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU path designated to carry a protected service under normal conditions.
reference.example: A fault on the working path causes selection of protection.

reference.label: protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU path reserved to protect the working path.
reference.example: AIS on the protection path removes redundancy while working traffic continues.

reference.label: active ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU path currently carrying the service, whether working or protection.
reference.example: After switchover, the protection route becomes the active ODU path.

reference.label: baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Standard monitoring available without an advanced optional telemetry package.
reference.example: Baseline monitoring provides alarms and 15-minute performance counters.

reference.label: optical-power monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring capability that exposes amplifier and receiver optical-power measurements.
reference.example: Enabling power monitoring adds amplifier input and output power values.

reference.label: optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring capability that provides per-channel power and OSNR at optical routing nodes.
reference.example: An OCM reports power and OSNR for channel 37 at a ROADM degree.

reference.label: advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Advanced telemetry exposing coherent-DSP quantities and equipment-health currents.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring reports pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, and laser bias.

reference.label: hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt failure that causes complete loss of traffic, signal, or equipment function.
reference.example: A fibre cut abruptly removes all traffic on the span.

reference.label: soft degradation
reference.definition: A condition in which traffic continues but signal or service quality is reduced.
reference.example: A 3 dB gain drop weakens channels without immediately stopping traffic.

reference.label: incipient failure
reference.definition: A slowly developing trend that precedes failure and may not yet affect traffic.
reference.example: Rising pump current indicates ageing before the amplifier loses service.

reference.label: transient event
reference.definition: A brief condition or disturbance lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: A short fibre disturbance causes a one-second power dip.

reference.label: critical severity
reference.definition: The highest operational alarm priority for immediate service or equipment failure.
reference.example: OTU frame loss is assigned critical severity because traffic cannot be recovered.

reference.label: major severity
reference.definition: A significant alarm priority below the highest failure level.
reference.example: Loss of span supervision is major even when payload traffic remains present.

reference.label: minor severity
reference.definition: A warning priority for degradation, ageing, or reduced resilience without immediate total failure.
reference.example: Pump end-of-life is minor while the amplifier still carries traffic.

reference.label: non-alarmed status
reference.definition: A reported condition retained for awareness but not assigned an actionable alarm priority.
reference.example: Receipt of propagated ODU AIS is logged as non-alarmed status.

reference.label: default condition handling
reference.definition: Handling applied to an arriving condition when no more specific rule covers it.
reference.example: An unrecognized incoming impairment follows the unit's default handling rule.

reference.label: transparent condition pass-through
reference.definition: A unit forwards an arriving condition or signal without terminating the condition.
reference.example: A noisy wavelength is routed onward and remains noisy.

reference.label: per-channel optical routing
reference.definition: A router independently switches each incoming wavelength to its configured outgoing direction.
reference.example: One east-arriving channel is routed north while another is routed west.

reference.label: receiver-side ODU protection selection
reference.definition: A receiving selector chooses between working and protection ODU routes for one service.
reference.example: When the working route fails, the destination selector switches to a clean protection route.

reference.label: span-local supervisory regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming supervisory link and originates a new link on the next span.
reference.example: Loss of the A–B OSC does not interrupt the independently originated B–C OSC.

reference.label: fixed-gain span compensation
reference.definition: An amplifier retains a commissioned gain chosen to offset the loss of its feeding span.
reference.example: An amplifier commissioned at 15 dB remains at 15 dB when span loss later rises.

reference.label: per-channel power equalization
reference.definition: A wavelength router adjusts individual channel powers toward a configured output launch level.
reference.example: Channels arriving at different powers are all launched onward near −4 dBm.

reference.label: downstream ODU AIS insertion
reference.definition: A transport endpoint inserts ODU AIS into downstream client ODUs after a server-layer failure.
reference.example: Loss of an aggregating OTU causes AIS insertion into all four carried ODUs.

reference.label: TRIB-FAIL alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating failure of the customer service on a tributary port.
reference.example: A tributary raises TRIB-FAIL after a fabric outage cuts its service.

reference.label: AIS-IN alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that a tributary port is receiving ODU AIS.
reference.example: A port receiving upstream AIS logs AIS-IN.

reference.label: REMOTE-AIS alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that the remote endpoint reports receiving ODU AIS from this side.
reference.example: The far tributary reports AIS and the local port raises REMOTE-AIS.

reference.label: TRACE-MISMATCH alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that an arriving ODU identity differs from the provisioned identity.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT-A receives CLIENT-B and raises TRACE-MISMATCH.

reference.label: ON-STANDBY alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that a protected service is currently using its standby route.
reference.example: A primary-path fault triggers switchover and ON-STANDBY.

reference.label: STANDBY-LOST alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating failure of the standby ODU route and loss of protection redundancy.
reference.example: The primary remains active while failure of route S raises STANDBY-LOST.

reference.label: TRIB-HW alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm for a physical hardware defect in a local tributary interface.
reference.example: A failed client-interface ASIC raises TRIB-HW.

reference.label: FABRIC-HW alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm for a physical hardware defect in the local ODU switching fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric card raises FABRIC-HW on the cross-connect.

reference.label: incoming-dark alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating absent incoming optical light at an amplifier or terminal.
reference.example: A cut span causes SEC-IN-DARK at the landing amplifier and RX-DARK at the terminal.

reference.label: SV-LOSS alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating loss of the incoming supervisory link on a fibre span.
reference.example: A severed span prevents supervisory reception and raises SV-LOSS.

reference.label: OUT-DARK alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that an optical amplifier emits no output light.
reference.example: A powered-off booster amplifier raises OUT-DARK.

reference.label: GAIN-DEV alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating that measured amplifier gain differs materially from its configured setting.
reference.example: An amplifier set for 18 dB delivers 15.5 dB and raises GAIN-DEV.

reference.label: PUMP-EOL alarm
reference.definition: A vendor alarm indicating pump drive has crossed its end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: An amplifier reaches 122% of commissioning pump drive and raises PUMP-EOL.

reference.label: FRAME-LOSS alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm indicating loss of OTU frame recovery.
reference.example: Low OSNR prevents frame recovery and the terminal raises FRAME-LOSS.

reference.label: DEGRADE alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm indicating that pre-FEC errors exceed the degradation threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER above threshold and triggers DEGRADE.

reference.label: REMOTE-DEFECT alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm indicating that the far end reported a defect in the locally transmitted signal.
reference.example: A backward defect indication causes the local terminal to raise REMOTE-DEFECT.

reference.label: TX-HW alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm identifying a hardware fault in the local transmit laser subsystem.
reference.example: A failed laser driver raises TX-HW.

reference.label: MOD-HW alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm identifying hardware failure of the local wavelength module.
reference.example: A module-controller failure raises MOD-HW and stops telemetry.

reference.label: TX-BIAS alarm
reference.definition: A vendor terminal alarm indicating transmit-laser bias above its ageing threshold.
reference.example: Laser bias reaches 124% of its commissioning value and raises TX-BIAS.
